rs.s1.lede: The odor fingerprint of human milk
rs.s3.lede: Reading GC-O-MS results from an electronic nose
rs.s4.lede: From fatty acids back to infant formula
rs.s1.cap: An electronic nose measured 303 human milk samples and 20 groups of animal milk (1,303 in total). Human and animal milk separate clearly, but human milk from six cities overlaps. Maternal lipid and protein intake show a stronger association with the odor fingerprint than region does.
rs.s2.cap: Sensory evaluation and GC-O-MS compare human milk, infant formula and five animal milks, and ROAV identifies the key flavor compounds that set them apart.
rs.s3.cap: Fast electronic-nose signals are used to predict the key flavor compounds found by GC-O-MS: the 14 sensor signals are compressed first, then six models are combined with weights set per compound.
rs.s4.cap: Ranking fatty acids and free amino acids in human milk: linoleic and α-linolenic acid are most strongly associated with its flavor, while free amino acids matter little. This gives a basis for adjusting the fatty acid profile of infant formula.

rs.m1.lede: From composition to a flavor score
rs.m2.lede: Turning time points into a curve
rs.m3.lede: From 25 experiments to the whole formulation space
rs.m1.cap: Beef tallow residue was hydrolyzed with five enzymes and then used in the Maillard reaction, and GC×GC-MS identified 49 main volatile compounds. A neural network predicts sensory scores from compound contents; a model that considers several compounds at once is more accurate than one that looks at a single compound, showing that flavors interact. Combined hydrolysis with Flavourzyme and papain gave the strongest meaty note.
rs.m2.cap: Beef tallow residue was hydrolyzed for 0 to 8 h before the Maillard reaction, and GC-O-MS with ROAV identified nine key flavor compounds, with the strongest roast note at 4 h. Three methods were compared for linking the five time points into a curve: polynomial fitting is not smooth, spline interpolation oscillates at both ends and goes negative, and the curve prediction model is smooth, never negative and has the smallest error in validation.
rs.m3.cap: Nine of 17 amino acids were selected, Latin hypercube sampling designed 25 combinations, and a neural network learned to predict six sensory attributes. The gap to the target flavor and the material cost are then combined into a total score to pick the best ratio from all combinations, followed by experimental validation.
